exposure: Gestational age at birth (late preterm vs. term)
outcome: Developmental delay at 4 years of age
cohort: 163 late preterm infants (47 complicated and 116 uncomplicated) compared to 158 term-born infants
finding: Late preterm infants with complications at birth, particularly respiratory morbidity, had a higher risk of communication delay at 4 years of age compared to term-born infants.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of developmental delay, specifically in the gross motor domain.
